angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,221,649.2 km at 189.04 pc = 0.086 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is published; the disc is far too small to resolve.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.2899 +/- 0.0826 mas (photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv), no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: 1.756 +/- 0.071 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (Ehrenreich et al. 2020, Nature 580, 597; arXiv:2003.05528, Extended Data Table 1, from their ESPRESSO spectra and the Gaia DR2 parallax). GM from their stellar mass 1.458 +/- 0.021 solar masses (same table) times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. The star has a bound companion, WASP-76 B, 0.44 arcsec away and about ten times fainter (same paper, Methods); it is not placed. presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the star's spin axis is not measured in three dimensions (Ehrenreich et al. 2020 measure only its sky-projected angle to the orbit, 61 degrees).
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ehrenreich et al. (2020), Nature 580, 597, Extended Data Table 1: 6,329 +/- 65 K from their ESPRESSO spectra (https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05528)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json), because no image of the photosphere exists (see investigations.json).
